NOT IMPLEMENTED and not previously listed. It is the layer between the compressed index and the histogram launch: Build() (:132-166) regroups each policy's features into up-to-four 5/6/7/8-bit SPECIALIZATION blocks by each group's own maxFolds (:111-124), where gbdt/gpu_data/feature_blocks.mojo emits ONE block per policy and greedy_search_helper dispatches at the whole block's widest fold count. Inert on a fold-count-HOMOGENEOUS dataset, which is every bench/oracle*.txt fixture and covtype -- which is why 288 of 288 never saw it. On a heterogeneous one-byte policy a single 200-fold feature drags every one-byte feature onto the 8-bit path. Also carries the score-tie exposure: their regrouping reorders bin features and compute_scores.cu:380 is a strict `if (gain < bestScore)`, so the lowest index wins a tie.

NOT IMPLEMENTED. `config.ForceOneBlockPerPolicy = statCount <= 2; config.StreamCount = statCount <= 2 ? 1 : 3` (:383-386). statCount is objective.GetDim() + 1, so MULTICLASS reaches the >2 arm and takes our single-stream one-block-per-policy path anyway. Metal has one queue (DEVIATION 119 covers streams generally, not this site).

NOT IMPLEMENTED. Reached only at ELoadFromCompressedIndexPolicy::GatherBins, which split_properties_helper.cpp:1338-1340 selects when leaves > 1 AND statCount > 2 -- i.e. multiclass. Reads the same bins in the same leaf order as LoadByIndexBins, so the histogram VALUES should agree; the multi-block split that accompanies it can move score ties.

NOT IMPLEMENTED. split_properties_helper.cpp:1098-1105 launches a distinct kernel family when leavesToCompute.size() == 1, which is every tree's ROOT level. Same arithmetic, same partition, so no model change; the cost is that their one-byte single-leaf arm divides CeilDivide(2 * maxActiveBlocks, ...) (hist_one_byte.cu:425-428) where the multi-part arm uses plain maxActiveBlocks, so at depth 0 we launch half the replicas they do.

PARTIALLY reflected in gbdt/gpu_data/compressed_index_builder.mojo, and one step is ABSENT: :43-50 does Shuffle(TRandom(0)) then std::sort by GetGroupingLevel for the OneByte policy, which exists specifically to cluster the <=128-bin features together (feature_layout.cpp:60-71, their own comment says it is for the no-atomics path). Ours walks input order. This is what makes their per-group specialization pay, so omitting it and compute_by_blocks_helper together means every one-byte feature runs at the widest width present.

column2: SetLeavesEstimationDefault's `if (treeConfig.L2Reg == 0.0f) { treeConfig.L2Reg = 1e-20f; }` (:357-359) for an explicit l2_leaf_reg=0
column3: gbdt/options/catboost_options.mojo::l2_leaf_reg_effective restates it and nothing calls it, so an explicit 0 reaches the fit as 0. Read effect: the Float32 leaf Hessian `w + l2` (leaves_estimation.mojo) gives the same bits (an empty leaf is 0 on both sides; `w + 1e-20` rounds to `w`); the Float64 walker lambda (`_estimate_and_apply`) can differ in the last bits for a leaf whose der2 sum is below about 1e-4. The structure searchers' scores were not audited for it. Applying it could move the recorded l2=0 cells (tools/e2_matrix_fit.py gbdt_rmse_l2reg0, checks/min_split_gain_binding.py, checks/min_child_hessian_binding.py), so it is recorded here; YetiRank, whose default is 0, applies it
